movesets.name: Bulk Up
movesets.description:
Running 20 Speed EVs lets Scrafty outspeed uninvested Grimmsnarl. Tera Poison inverts Scrafty's glaring 4x Fairy weakness, denies Fighting-type revenge killers such as Pawmot, and protects it from Toxic, but it also leaves Scrafty vulnerable to Psychic-type coverage from the likes of Bruxish and Florges. Tera Fairy is another option that still helps out against Fighting-types without leaving Scrafty weak to attackers like Hoopa and Rhydon, though the newfound Poison weakness gives Scrafty a harder time getting around threats like Salazzle and Amoonguss.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

movesets.name: Dragon Dance
movesets.description:
Poison Jab threatens Florges with heavy damage and receives a power boost from Tera Poison, while Encore can be used to disrupt passive foes such as Milotic and generate additional setup turns. Scrafty can opt for bulkier EV spreads to give it an easier time setting up, but doing so cuts into Scrafty's damage output, which can complicate sweeping. strategies.overview: Thanks to its solid mixed bulk, many resistances, and great abilities, Scrafty is a potent setup sweeper. Both Bulk Up and Dragon Dance sets are major setup threats because of Scrafty's access to STAB Knock Off, Close Combat, and Drain Punch for great overall power, utility, and sustainability. Staple Pokemon like Alolan Muk and Amoonguss can be setup fodder for Scrafty, letting it prey on common defensive cores. Bulk Up turns Scrafty into a bulky booster that can overwhelm defensive cores relying on Swampert and Bronzong. Dragon Dance sets can snowball out of control and use Scrafty's great bulk to secure multiple boosts. Scrafty is an especially good user of Terastallization, as it's bulky and enabled by flipping its few major weaknesses into resistances. Shed Skin is a fantastic ability to make status users like Vaporeon and Galarian Slowbro insecure checks to Scrafty, and Scrafty even has other good abilities like Intimidate and Moxie to facilitate its sweeping. However, Scrafty has major vulnerabilities to Fairy-types like Diancie and Scream Tail and Fighting-type revenge killers like Paldean Tauros-W and Paldean Tauros-F, so it's often pressured to exhaust Terastallization. Dragon Dance sets can struggle if they don't have the opportunity to acquire multiple boosts, and Bulk Up sets can be overwhelmed by strong special attackers like Toxtricity and Sylveon. Scrafty's low Speed trips it up by making it vulnerable to Encore and Taunt, and its average Attack makes it even more prone to Trick and phazing.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Ice Punch hits Flying- and Dragon-types like Altaria, Gligar, and Flygon very hard, but Scrafty struggles to fit it for this one matchup over its coverage moves for Fairy-types. Tera Ghost is an option for a useful immunity against Fighting-types like Paldean Tauros-W and Body Press users like Bronzong, potentially turning them into setup fodder or giving Scrafty a critical turn where it doesn't have to take any damage when it's weakened.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Diancie can OHKO Scrafty with Moonblast and is capable of beating it with Body Press and boosts from Diamond Storm. However, Diancie can be overwhelmed due to its dependence on Leftovers for recovery and lack of Fighting resistance. Klefki can force Bulk Up sets to either Terastallize or fall to Dazzling Gleam, but Dragon Dance Scrafty can threaten to OHKO Klefki with +1 Close Combat after Spikes damage. Calm Mind and lead Scream Tail variants can both beat Scrafty, but utility sets are setup fodder for Dragon Dance Scrafty. Fairy-types like Sylveon and Florges and Tera Fairy users like Uxie and Milotic should stay wary of Scrafty's coverage moves.

Fighting-types: Flamigo, Toxicroak, and Heracross all deal major damage to Scrafty with their STAB moves and resist both of Scrafty's STAB types. Paldean Tauros-F and Paldean Tauros-W can run Choice Scarf to outspeed Dragon Dance Scrafty variants, and they both soften it up with Intimidate. Breloom and Infernape can both pick off weakened Scrafty with Mach Punch.

Flying-types: Scyther, Galarian Articuno, and Kilowattrel both outspeed and threaten Scrafty with their super effective STAB attacks, and the last one even outspeeds Jolly Scrafty at +1. Neither of these Pokemon, or most Flying-types in general, enjoy switching into Knock Off. Gligar can beat Dragon Dance sets in a vacuum, but it can lose to Bulk Up sets. Trapper Altaria sets can remove Scrafty with Perish Song.

Poison-types: Toxicroak and Amoonguss both resist Scrafty's Fighting-type moves; Toxicroak can hit Scrafty back hard with Fighting-type moves, and Amoonguss is bulky enough to chip down Scrafty with Sludge Bomb and Giga Drain. However, Amoonguss can lose to Shed Skin Bulk Up Scrafty sets.

Item Removal and Disruption: Chandelure, Munkidori, and Meloetta can cripple Scrafty with a Choice item if they're not able to KO it, leaving it exploitable. Fast Encore users like Scream Tail, Cinccino, and Uxie can force Scrafty to repeatedly set up or use Rest, which enables them and their teammates to begin exploiting it.

movesets.name: Bulk Up
movesets.description:
Set Details

Drain Punch's healing makes Scrafty less reliant on Rest. Knock Off is especially useful to soften up Gligar and punish Scrafty's checks, including Scyther, Diancie, and Altaria. Throat Chop stops Sylveon from using Hyper Voice and prevents Bronzong from using Psychic Noise if Scrafty has Terastallized into a Poison-type. Rest is less passive on Scrafty than other Pokemon thanks to Shed Skin's potential to wake up Scrafty early, and it's helpful both as a recovery move and immediate method to heal status. The EV spread allows Scrafty to outpace foes like Vaporeon and Sylveon. Shed Skin has good synergy with Rest and keeps Scrafty healthier against status spreaders like Alolan Muk, Gligar, and Vaporeon. Both Tera Poison and Tera Steel flip Scrafty's problematic 4x Fairy weakness into a resistance, which improves its matchups against Diancie, Sylveon, and Scream Tail. Tera Poison helps Scrafty against Fighting-types like Toxicroak and opposing Scrafty, while Tera Steel is more useful against Alolan Ninetales and Kilowattrel.

Scrafty is unlikely to sweep unless Fairy-types like Scream Tail, Florges, and Sylveon have been weakened. Bronzong, Klefki, and Orthworm check Fairy-types for Scrafty, and they can set entry hazards to wear down Diancie and Amoonguss. Ground-types like Flygon, Gastrodon, and Swampert can handle Poison-types like Toxtricity and Toxicroak for Scrafty. Spikes setters like Klekfi, Gligar, and Orthworm are especially good at making sure foes like Amoonguss are softened up for Scrafty, and Scrafty's Knock Off synergizes with them by removing Heavy-Duty Boots. Specially defensive Pokemon like Diancie, Bronzong, and Porygon2 are great answers to problematic special attackers like Alolan Ninetales, Kilowattrel, and Chandelure that can pressure Scrafty with their super effective and powerful STAB moves, and the former two walls can set up hazards for Scrafty as well. Physical walls like Galarian Slowbro, Vaporeon, and Gligar support Scrafty by handling physical attackers like Paldean Tauros-F, Incineroar, and Flamigo.

movesets.name: Dragon Dance
movesets.description:
Set Details

Drain Punch helps keep Scrafty healthy enough to stay out of range of priority users like Basculegion-M and Choice Scarf revenge killers like Flygon. Knock Off can be helpful to soften up checks to Scrafty such as Scream Tail, Gligar, and Sylveon so that Scrafty can more easily sweep past them late-game. Throat Chop lacks Knock Off's general utility and initial additional power, but its effect of disabling sound-based moves helps against foes like Sylveon and Toxtricity. Scrafty can run Encore to navigate around problematic foes like Milotic and Vaporeon, and it can turn passive walls like Avalugg and Amoonguss into setup fodder. Poison Jab is preferred as a coverage move for its synergy with Tera Poison, but Iron Head nails Alolan Ninetales and Diancie. Similarly to Drain Punch, Leftovers helps keep Scrafty out of range of revenge killers like Basculegion-M. However, a Lum Berry is very helpful for non-Shed Skin sets to help against status spreaders like Gligar, Incineroar, and Klefki if Scrafty Terastallizes. Shed Skin makes Scrafty less prone to status spreaders like Incineroar, Gligar, and Alolan Muk, which can also open Scrafty up to use these Pokemon as setup fodder. Intimidate creates windows for Scrafty to set up more easily against physical attackers like Flygon and Swampert. Moxie helps Scrafty to snowball with boosts and punish opponents who eagerly sack Pokemon against it. Tera Poison helps Scrafty match up better against Fairy-types, Fighting-type revenge killers like Paldean Tauros-W, and Body Press users such as Bronzong. Tera Steel shares Tera Poison's offensive and defensive qualities against Fairy-types while giving Scrafty a better defensive typing against Flying-types like Kilowattrel and Psychic-types like Uxie.

Scrafty is a good fit for offense and balance teams as a wincon that isn't lacking a defensive backbone. Sets with Shed Skin are especially valuable as status absorbers. Scrafty can take advantage of Alolan Muk, which is appreciated by Psychic-types like Scream Tail, Oricorio-P, and Bronzong. Psychic-type pivots like Munkidori and Uxie are excellent at drawing in Alolan Muk for Scrafty and giving it free entry with their pivot moves. Setup sweepers like Flygon, Scyther, and Diancie can all overwhelm Fairy- and Poison-type walls for Scrafty. In return, Scrafty can beat Steel-types like Bronzong for the three aforementioned Pokemon. Fast Encore users like Scream Tail and Cinccino can lock passive Pokemon like Bronzong and Amoonguss into moves that let Scrafty use them as setup fodder. Alolan Ninetales supports Scrafty with Aurora Veil and Encore to widen its opportunities for setting up. Steel- and Poison-type teammates like Klefki and Toxtricity can handle Fairy-types like Scream Tail and Sylveon.

movesets.name: Bulk Up (Fighting)
movesets.description:
Scrafty makes the difference in the Dragon and Ghost matchups. Thanks to its Psychic-type immunity and good special bulk, it can tank special moves from Choice Specs Dragapult, Latios, and Gholdengo, while Shed Skin allows Scrafty to absorb status for the team. With Bulk Up, Scrafty enhances both its offensive and defensive utility and becomes able to win its duel against Archaludon. Drain Punch recovers part of the damage it inflicts and synergizes well with Bulk Up, while Knock Off deals with Psychic- and Ghost-type targets that Drain Punch does not cover such as Latios, Galarian Slowking, Dragapult, and Gholdengo. Combined with Shed Skin, Rest becomes a reliable recovery move and lets Scrafty withstand multiple powerful special moves from the likes of Greninja, Latios, and Dragapult; with a Careful nature, Scrafty is only 3HKOed by Latios's Draco Meteor.

Scrafty is well supported by Great Tusk, which can clear entry hazards from the field, set Stealth Rock, and use Knock Off to remove items such as Leftovers and Rocky Helmet from the likes of Corviknight and Garchomp. In return, Scrafty can take special moves from Dragapult and Latios. Assault Vest Iron Hands and Gallade are two prominent partners that can ease Scrafty's defensive burden for the team while also threatening out Fairy-type Pokemon like Iron Valiant and Primarina that it cannot hurt significantly. Iron Hands can especially make the difference in the Flying and Water matchups by removing Tornadus-T, Choice Scarf Enamorus, Choice Specs Kingdra, and Primarina. Gallade, on the other hand, improves the Fighting and Poison matchups, as it slashes through Keldeo, Iron Valiant, Toxapex, and Galarian Weezing. By virtue of its more defensive role, Scrafty needs to be surrounded by powerful wallbreakers that can make progress in the game like Sneasler, Iron Valiant, Urshifu-R, and Keldeo. Choice Scarf Sneasler provides an offensive check to Fairy-type foes such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Iron Valiant and can cripple Toxapex with Switcheroo, while Unburden Sneasler is a great finisher in the Fairy and Dragon matchups. Iron Valiant puts the pressure on the Steel, Flying, and Water defensive cores, easily disposing of Skarmory, Gliscor, defensive Gyarados, and Toxapex. It also synergizes well with Scrafty defensively by providing a Dragon immunity to shut down both Choice Specs Dragapult and Latios. Lastly, Urshifu-R and Keldeo are both solid options to improve specific matchups like the Ground and Dark matchups, respectively, destroying their offensive and defensive cores with their STAB combination.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 7 onwards

Price Range: 6-7 points

Overview: Scrafty is a versatile Pokemon with three solid abilities and a wide movepool that can help it fill many roles, whether that role is sweeping with Dragon Dance and Moxie, absorbing hits with its high defenses and Intimidate and providing utility with the likes of Knock Off and Encore, or absorbing status with Shed Skin. However, Scrafty's relatively low Speed, HP, and Attack mean it can have difficulty in all of these roles and needs a lot of support to find success.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Tank: With its high defenses, Scrafty can switch into many attacks and threaten foes out with moves like Close Combat. It also has access to Knock Off to help deal with items, Super Fang for flat damage allowing it to maximize its defensive capabilities, and useful utility moves like Taunt and Encore.

Setup Sweeper: With Dragon Dance and its naturally high defenses, Scrafty can become a threatening sweeper if not answered properly. Alternatively, Bulk Up and Swords Dance can be used on sets aiming to outlive foes instead of outspeed them.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Close Combat, Drain Punch, Knock Off, Crunch, Low Kick

Setup Moves: Dragon Dance, Swords Dance, Bulk Up

Utility Moves: Rest, Taunt, Encore, Substitute, Brick Break, Dragon Tail, Super Fang, Roar

Coverage: Dragon Claw, Fire Punch, Ice Punch, Iron Head, Head Smash, Poison Jab, Stone Edge, Thunder Punch, Zen Headbutt

Niche Moves

Upper Hand: While priority is usually not necessary to move first against Scrafty, Upper Hand can catch Choice-locked foes or foes without better options off guard.

Common Items

Leftovers: Scrafty values longevity in most games, and Leftovers helps Scrafty stay on the field longer.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Ignoring entry hazard damage allows Scrafty to switch in more, which can help in games where it is forced out easily.

Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet allows Scrafty to punish foes using physical attacks, and Scrafty makes a good switch-in to Knock Off due to its good natural bulk.

Assault Vest: With its wide array of coverage moves, Scrafty can make good use of Assault Vest to be even tankier specially without losing much value.

Niche Items

Resistance Berries: Scrafty usually needs to take a hit or two while setting up, and resistance Berries such as Roseli and Chople Berry can allow it to gain the boosts it needs to accomplish a sweep.

Other Damage-boosting Items: While Scrafty usually values the longevity provided by other items, with its wide array of coverage moves, it can make good use of Expert Belt, and Life Orb can boost its damage output when longevity is less necessary.

Tera

Scrafty can make for a versatile secondary Tera Captain; shedding its weakness-riddled Dark and Fighting types for a more defensively sound Tera type like Tera Water or Fairy can do wonders for it. Alternatively, offensive sets can benefit from using Tera Steel or Poison to flip matchups on foes and boost the power of their coverage moves. However, Scrafty's mediocre stats mean Terastallization cannot solve all of its shortcomings.

Draft Strategy

Scrafty can fulfill a variety of roles, being able to set up and sweep or disrupt with moves like Knock Off and Encore. However, Scrafty should be an auxiliary piece on a solid draft and not a necessary part of a plan. That being said, it appreciates teammates that can bring it in safely and help chip down foes.

Pivots: Scrafty benefits greatly from teammates like Tornadus-T and Rotom-W that can scout foes' moves and bring it in safely.

Entry Hazard Setters: Whether setting up or filling a more defensive role, (AC) Scrafty forces switches and removes Heavy-Duty Boots from foes, so keeping entry hazards up with teammates like Gliscor and Glimmora can let it make good progress throughout a game.

Fairy-resistant Pokemon: Scrafty's 4x weakness to Fairy and inability to hit Fairy-types very hard means it can allow opposing Fairy-type Pokemon in easily. Pokemon like Iron Treads and Galarian Slowking make good partners for switching into the Fairy-type attacks Scrafty baits out.

Sweepers: With its ability to use Knock Off many times throughout a game, Scrafty can remove Heavy-Duty Boots and other pesky items to make it easier for sweepers like Greninja and Iron Valiant to do their job.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Fairy-types resist Scrafty's STAB moves and hit it for 4x damage, so Pokemon like Enamorus and even Pokemon using Tera Fairy like Raging Bolt make it very hard for Scrafty to stick around for long.

Physically Defensive Foes: While Scrafty has many setup options and a decent defensive profile, its low base Attack means Pokemon like Great Tusk and Corviknight can switch into it with relative ease and force it out.

Disruption: With its low Speed, t can be very easy for foes to use Encore to force Scrafty into useless moves or use Taunt before Scrafty can use its status moves.

Status: While Scrafty gets access to Shed Skin, which can help in some matchups, on sets not using Shed Skin, status conditions like burn and paralysis can be quite annoying to deal with.
